HomeEssentials Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer; David Kwon, Chief Stores Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the second quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Our brick-and-mortar foundation remains resilient, enhanced by strong omnichannel execution as we tackle softer consumer traffic and inflationary pressures. Total net sales hit $2.82 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year, marking our eighth straight quarter of growth and beating our guidance midpoint by 150 basis points, even against a tough comparable-store sales backdrop industry-wide. Comps rose 3.1% overall, outpacing the Retail Metrics Index's +1.2% for home goods retailers. Store traffic increased 2.8%, powered by our Essentials Everyday loyalty program with 28 million active members, up 12% year-over-year, lifting conversion rates to 24.5%, a 90 basis point gain.

In core categories, appliances comped +4.7% on demand for energy-efficient models amid higher utility costs, with average unit retail up 2.3% from a premium mix shift toward brands like Whirlpool and GE. Furniture and décor grew 3.9% comps, driven by our private-label HomeForge line, capturing 18% market share per Nielsen and 22% of total furniture sales. Home improvement softened to +1.2% comps due to housing headwinds like 7% mortgage rates, but we beat peers like Home Depot's flat performance there.

E-commerce, now 14% of sales and up 22% year-over-year, amplified our store synergy. BOPIS orders jumped 35%, making up 42% of digital sales, optimizing fulfillment across our 1,250 stores and cutting shipping costs 15%. Marketplace ties with Amazon and Walmart+ added $180 million in revenue.

Gross margins expanded 110 basis points to 36.4%, our best Q2 in five years, thanks to supply chain moves like our AI inventory system in 85% of distribution centers, boosting turns to 5.8x from 5.2x and reducing stockouts 28%. Freight costs eased 60 basis points post-rate hikes, markdowns optimized to 2.1% of sales from 2.7%, and shrink held at 1.4% via RFID pilots in 200 high-theft stores.

SG&A deleveraged 40 basis points to 22.1% with payroll efficiencies from labor scheduling tech, cutting overtime 17%. Adjusted operating income rose 14% to $285 million, EBITDA up 18% to $410 million at 14.6% margins. Diluted EPS hit $1.12, topping our $0.98-$1.04 guide and up 22% year-over-year. Free cash flow shone at $320 million, supporting $150 million in repurchases under our $2 billion program and a 12% dividend increase to $0.28 per share.

Geographically balanced, Southeast and Midwest led with +4.2% comps in our 420 stores, aided by weather and reno tailwinds in Florida and Texas. Northeast comps at +1.8% improved via 15 new small-format stores in dense areas like Boston and Philly, hitting +6%. West Coast flat at +0.9% got a lift from pop-up shops boosting traffic 11%. Our 50-store Canada pilot grew 9%, eyeing 20 more in 2025.

These results affirm our store-centric omnichannel strategy, with $250 million YTD in remodels adding experiential zones like kitchen demos, driving +8.2% comps in those stores. Our Snowflake-powered data lake personalizes 70% of SKUs, upping sell-through 15%. We're guiding Q3 comps +2.0% to +3.5%, sales $2.75 billion to $2.85 billion, EPS $1.05-$1.15, on track for full-year comps over 3%.

We're leveraging our physical stores' convenience with digital enhancements to lead the industry. Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the second quarter.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.82 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 36.4%, expanding 110 basis points year-over-year, primarily driven by favorable product mix, supply chain efficiencies, lower freight costs, and optimized markdowns. To elaborate on that margin strength, it marks our third straight quarter of expansion and positions us at the high end of guidance. This outperforms the retail average around 35% per the National Retail Federation and narrows the gap with leaders like Costco. The lift came from owned brands at 28% of sales, up from 22%, delivering mid-50s margins versus 32% on vendor apparel. Freight moderated to a 20 basis point drag from 150 last year via multi-year Maersk and UPS deals, cutting ocean costs 12% and rail shifts saving 8%. Shrink improved to 1.1% from 1.6% with RFID in 65% of stores, reducing out-of-stocks 22% and markdowns 40 basis points to 4.2%. Sunbelt margins hit 40.1%, up 280 basis points on new formats, while Northeast gained 180 despite costs via localized pricing.

On markdowns specifically, they rose modestly but strategically to manage inventory up 4% entering Q2, skewed to warm-weather apparel. At 14.8% of sales versus 12.6% last year, they accounted for 110 basis points of pressure, totaling $128 million. Apparel clearance hit 22%, reflecting soft demand and fast-fashion competition, peaking at 18.2% mid-quarter before tapering to 11.5%. Northeast contained at 13.2%, Sunbelt higher at 17.5% from weather. Ex-markdowns, merchandise margin held at 41.7%, up 10 basis points on private labels at 28% penetration. We've countered with RetailFlow AI in 65% of stores for 12% less excess inventory and dynamic pricing, targeting 13-14% markdowns in Q3 for 39.5-40.0% margins.

Operating expenses were $625 million, representing 22.1% of revenue. Marketing and advertising expenses totaled $162 million, up 12% year-over-year or 4.8% of sales, investing in high-ROI channels to drive traffic amid mall declines. Digital took 58% at $94 million, up 28%, with Google, Meta, TikTok yielding 5.8x ROAS on ForgeMart Fix-Up via Adobe Sensei. CTV at 15% boosted traffic 18%, traditional down 8%. Sunbelt spend up 22% at 4.7x ROAS, Northeast flat. Our CDP ingests 1.2 billion signals for precise LTV, shifting to retargeting. H2 at 4.7-4.9% of sales, digital over 65%, ROAS 4.5x.

Net income was $200 million, or $1.12 per share. We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently optimized with 5.8x turns, down from prior, supporting working capital release.

We're maintaining a strong balance sheet and well positioned to invest in growth. Looking to outlook, Q3 revenue $2.75 billion to $2.85 billion, comps 2.0-3.5%, EPS $1.05-$1.15. Full-year comps over 3%, revenue $11.4-$11.6 billion, EPS $3.85-$3.95, FCF $650-$700 million. Q4 comps 2.5-4.5%, digital 8-10%, margins 38.2-38.5% on owned brands to 42%, SG&A 26.0-26.4%. Sunbelt 5-7%, international 4%. Risks include delinquencies, but tech like RFID at 92% cuts shrink to 0.9%.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Patel, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by David Kwon to discuss store operations, Emily Vargas to discuss marketing initiatives, and Raj Singh to talk about technology advancements.

Lisa Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Michael. This quarter, we launched expansions to our HomeForge private-label line, which gained 18% market share and drove 22% of furniture sales, with strong comps of 3.9%. Owned brands now at 28% penetration deliver superior margins, and we're excited about upcoming sustainable drops like recycled bedding, targeting mid-50s margins. We've rationalized low-performers, boosting mix toward high-ASP furniture.

David Kwon, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. As part of our Store of the Future strategy, we're accelerating remodels: 150 stores this year at $375 million capex, up 76% from 85 last year, planning 200 annually through 2026 for over 550 total. Early cohorts show +14.2% comps versus flat system-wide, with 9% traffic lift, 12% conversion, $78 baskets, $650 AUV. Playbook includes wider 8-foot aisles, speed zones for private labels up 22%, MaxTech self-checkout at 65% transactions, AR mirrors lifting apparel 15%, BOPIS lockers under 2 minutes. Sustainability via LEDs saving 40% energy, solar, EV chargers, zero-waste dispensers up 10%. Experiential like Starbucks shops extend dwell to 28 minutes, localized patios in Sunbelt for $700+ AUV. Sunbelt +17% comps, Midwest +11%. Payback 24-30 months, 25% IRR, funding organically while pruning laggards.

Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, David. Our Essentials Everyday campaign has increased brand awareness and loyalty, with 28 million members driving conversion gains. Marketing at 4.8% of sales emphasizes digital acceleration for traffic and omnichannel, with ROAS up to 4.2x, geo-fencing tying to store visits amid showrooming.

Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer:
Thank you, Emily. We have invested in our Unified Commerce Platform and AI-driven supply chain, improving OTIF to 97.2%, turns to 7.6x, DIO to 48 days. DC automation with AGVs and Symbotic boosts throughput 35%, forecasting error down 42% via Palantir-NielsenIQ. Real-time inventory 98% accurate, app scan-and-fulfill at 42% adoption, AI orchestration for 88% same-day BOPIS. Omnichannel at 28% of digital, BOPIS 62% of that up 35% YoY, $1.2 billion GMV, 18% AOV lift to $145, curbside +52% at 4.2% costs. Halo effect up 12% traffic, 65% add-on buys. RFID shelves in 150 stores, 99.2% accuracy. $150 million capex for robots, voice commerce, targeting 35% digital mix.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflationary pressures on your sales?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has pressured big-ticket discretionary like appliances and furniture, with consumers trading down to value essentials comping mid-teens. However, our owned brands and loyalty program mitigated this, delivering 3.1% overall comps versus industry softness. Regional balance and omnichannel BOPIS helped capture convenience seekers, keeping traffic positive.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Maria. For Q3, we're guiding comps to 2.0% to 3.5%, with full-year north of 3%. This factors resilient traffic, digital acceleration to 8-10% in Q4, and remodel lift of 300 basis points. Sunbelt strength at 5-7% offsets softer Northeast, with holiday build and rate cut potential supporting.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, David. We've unlocked $285 million in run-rate savings, expanding margins 210 basis points. OTIF at 97.2% via $450 million in DC automation—AGVs, Symbotic robotics upping throughput 35%, cycle times to 10 hours. AI forecasting cut error 42%, DIO to 48 days, turns 7.6x, freeing $1.2 billion capital. Nearshoring 40% sourcing, rail shifts saved 28% freight. International micro-DCs improved 31%. This builds resilience against Red Sea issues, positioning for 50-75 bps more EBITDA lift.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Lisa. Essentials Everyday with 28 million members, up 12%, drove 2.8% traffic and 90 bps conversion to 24.5%. It boosts AOV via personalization, 25% higher baskets, halo from omnichannel. ROAS synergies with marketing, LTV $450 vs. $380 non-members. Key to outpacing comps in a tight wallet environment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Robert Hayes (Bank of America):
Thanks. On remodels, how does the ROI look amid capex ramp?

David Kwon, Chief Stores Officer:
Robert, ROI is strong at 24-30 month payback, over 25% IRR. Remodeled stores at +14.2% comps, 150 bps EBITDA expansion to 12.5%, private-label 42%. We're funding via FCF, balancing with closures, confident in 300 bps comp contribution.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes our Q&A. I'll now turn back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
